speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Films Act (FA) sets out the regulatory framework for the distribution, exhibition and possession of films in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The FA, therefore, ensures consumers can make informed choices about films and video games, protects the young from mature content and ensures that films do not undermine national harmony or security, or the public interest.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It was enacted nearly four decades ago in 1981 to replace the Cinematograph Films Act inherited from the British, and to deal with the advent of video tapes and discs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Since 1998, changes have also been made, for instance, to address the introduction of video compact discs (VCDs) and the spread of obscene films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The FA must, therefore, be updated to remain relevant for the films industry and consumers, but also to continue to safeguard the public interest.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The world today has changed significantly since 1998, 20 years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The films industry, the broader media landscape and the needs and demands of Singapore consumers have evolved.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There are three key trends that underpin our proposed amendments.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First, our films industry has grown more vibrant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Second, technological developments continue to spur changes in film distribution and consumption.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Film exhibitors no longer need physical or digital copies of a film to screen it.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Instead, the film can be stored remotely, locally or overseas, and streamed over the Internet to a public screening in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Digital cinema, as this is known, is already a reality in the United States (US).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Video games are also becoming more visually realistic, increasingly featuring mature themes, such as violence, gore and sex.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The broader media environment has also shifted as a result of digital advances.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We live in an era of media pervasiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This gives Singaporeans greater viewing and entertainment choices, but we also have to remain vigilant against content that could weaken our security, stability or unity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Around the world, we have seen a sharp rise in content that spreads discord, extremism and hatred, as well as information campaigns that seek to interfere in elections or the affairs of other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: While such activities can take the form of tweets and posts, they can also take the form of films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Third, our society has become more educated and mature, even as the film and media landscape has grown more dynamic and complex.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Coupled with the subjective nature of how films can impact viewers and society, this means that what constitutes appropriate or inappropriate content today could be different tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA should, therefore, have the means to reconsider and update classification-related decisions, especially those that were made many years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MCI and IMDA have also engaged the films industry and community since late 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We have received much useful feedback and have modified some of our proposals.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our goal is to make the films regulatory regime more business- and consumer-friendly, while ensuring that it remains relevant and effective going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The first set of amendments seeks to formalise the co-classification scheme, which we have piloted since 2011 for video distribution, and 2015 for film exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Sections 19 to 20C of the Bill will formalise this scheme by setting out the registration requirements for film CAs, the types of films they can classify, the duties of the film CAs, and the regulatory steps that may be taken against misclassification.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The co-classification scheme will nurture a pool of CAs familiar with the film classification guidelines and enable films and videos to be brought to the market more quickly, thereby benefiting both film exhibitors and distributors, as well as consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will put in place safeguards to ensure that our content standards are upheld.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I would also clarify that the scheme is optional.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Industry players will get an additional option for film classification, but those who prefer to submit films to IMDA for classification can continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The second set of amendments seeks to clarify the FA's regulatory scope in four areas.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The current FA requires all films to be classified.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Anyone who wishes to import, make, distribute or exhibit a film will also need to be licensed by IMDA, unless exempted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Going forward, the type of activities to be regulated will be reduced.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First, the Act will be amended to reflect IMDA's focus on the distribution and public exhibition of films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clauses 7 and 11, therefore, clarify that licensing and classification will only apply to the distribution and public exhibition of films henceforth.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Section 6 is amended to remove the making and private exhibition of films from the FA’s licensing scope.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Section 21 is similarly amended so that films meant for private consumption no longer need to be classified.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, IMDA will still be able to require a film to be submitted for classification.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For instance, IMDA may receive feedback that a film contains content that could undermine public interest and would thus require the film for review.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This provides a balance between protecting the public and reducing regulatory reach.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such activities need not necessarily be carried out by cinemas or video retailers; one can easily purchase a DVD at a bookstore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our intent is to regulate the distribution and public exhibition of films consistently, regardless of the nature of the business.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our concern, Sir, is with the film activity and content, rather than the entity or person.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To focus IMDA's regulatory efforts further, we also intend to grant exemptions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For instance, there is currently no need to obtain a licence for the public exhibition of films that are classified up to PG13, and we are considering further exemptions for distribution and classification.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Third, with technological advances, an exhibitor in Singapore no longer requires the physical reel to screen a film.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A cinema operator can have the film digitally streamed from overseas for public exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 3 updates the definitions in section 2 to allow IMDA to regulate the public exhibition of films consistently, whether they are screened from a copy or via a transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Since online streaming has made film exhibition possible without a physical or digital copy, we also propose to amend section 35 to clarify that exhibiting prohibited films is also an offence, besides the possession and distribution of such films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will be able to impose licence conditions, such as specifying that retailers do not sell Mature 18 (M18) video games to underage patrons.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Since the class licence is automatic, video game retailers need not register, nor will there be licence fees or performance bonds.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It would be largely business as usual for these retailers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: First, a new section 15 will empower IMDA to reclassify films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Films are classified based on the film classification guidelines, which are updated from time to time to reflect our evolving norms and values.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A film classified in the past may thus qualify for a different classification rating today.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This amendment will enable IMDA to respond to new information or changes in the film classification guidelines by reviewing past classification decisions to keep them up to date.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A film may be reclassified to a higher or lower rating.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Should stakeholders be aggrieved by the reclassification, they may appeal to the Films Appeal Committee (FAC).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Second, a new section 28 will set out a new right of appeal to the Minister against IMDA's decision in areas other than classification, like refusing licensing, suspending or revoking licences or refusing to register a person as a film CA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This will bring the FA in line with other media laws which have such provisions and ensure that the industry has avenues of recourse for both classification and non-classification related decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Third, section 24, which deals with appeals against IMDA's classification decisions, will be amended to allow a broader group of appellants, so long as these persons have a nexus to the film.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This includes the person who applied for classification, the person who intends to distribute or publicly exhibit the film, the maker of the film, and the film CA whose classification rating has been overruled by IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Fourth, section 24 will also be amended for appeals against IMDA's decision to refuse classification for films that are against national security.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These appeals will henceforth be heard and decided by the Minister instead of FAC.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We have proposed this amendment as ensuring national security is one of the Government's core responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is neither ideal nor fair for a citizen panel, such as FAC, to assess threats to national security, as members may not be privy to the full extent of security concerns due to the sensitivity of the information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Notwithstanding this, section 24A requires the Minister to first consult with FAC before coming to a final decision, to preserve citizen representation in the deliberation of such appeals.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I would add that films are rarely disallowed on grounds of national security, but we need to be vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The amendment also takes into account the increasing pervasiveness of media and how different media, including film, can be used to disseminate content that could undermine our security.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The fourth set of amendments seeks to extend IMDA's enforcement and investigation powers for better administration of the Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I will elaborate on the need for these amendments as they received the most feedback during our public consultation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Besides protecting the young, films are also regulated to ensure that the content does not undermine the social fabric of our society, racial and religious harmony or national security.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is particularly critical, given our diverse, multiracial and multi-religious society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As one of the smallest and most open countries, we are also highly susceptible to foreign influences and information campaigns that can undermine our social values and sow discord among our communities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Advances in technology mean that such undesirable content can easily be disseminated locally, through the rapid and mass reproduction of films in thumbdrives, digital video disc (DVDs) or secure digital (SD) cards, or streamed from overseas for screening in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Issues like race and religion have torn many societies apart, but, in Singapore, we live together harmoniously.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This did not occur by chance, and we need to continue to work hard to preserve it.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Under the current FA, IMDA, as the licensing and classification authority, already has powers to enter premises and seize items that constitute evidence, without warrant, for serious offences, such as those involving obscene and unclassified films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These powers are vital to the protection of public interest so that IMDA is able to secure the necessary evidence for prosecution.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Without-warrant powers and the use of reasonable force to gain entry are crucial, given the ease of flight and the ease of removing evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, an ad hoc public exhibition of an unclassified film can be over in two hours or less, while thumbdrives and SD cards can be quickly and easily disposed of.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Second, IMDA has no powers to require information or record statements from persons who have knowledge of the offence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Today, even if IMDA seizes obscene or unclassified films under existing powers, the matter has to be passed over to the Police for investigations, despite IMDA having the requisite expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, for serious offences in the Act, such as those involving obscene and unclassified films, an IMDA enforcement officer can enter, search and seize evidence without warrant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The power to enter and search without warrant will only be exercised when the enforcement officer suspects on reasonable grounds that the specified offences have been committed or are being committed, or that evidence of the commission of the specified offences can be found in the relevant premises and it is necessary to secure the evidence to prevent it from being concealed, lost or destroyed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The new sections 23, 34 and 34A will enable IMDA to enforce the FA effectively and efficiently whenever necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They will also allow the Police to focus their resources on other threats to security and law and order.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We will also enhance the range of IMDA's regulatory actions so that it can better tailor regulatory responses to the severity of breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Section 11 is amended to widen the range of regulatory actions that can be taken against licensees for non-compliance with FA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For instance, IMDA will be able to act against a single outlet of a distributor for a breach, instead of penalising every outlet under the distributor.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Clause 2 amends the Act's long title to reflect the shift from censorship towards classification.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Sections 3 and 4 are amended to dissolve and transfer the functions of the Board of Film Censors (BFC) to IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This simply regularises the existing practice where the Minister has appointed IMDA officers to BFC since 2003.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Thus, there is no need to maintain a BFC structure that is distinct from IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There will be no knock-on changes to the classification processes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Several sections are amended to remove the minimum fines for various FA offences.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This will align FA with modern legislative practice which gives the Courts discretion to impose an appropriate sentence, unconstrained by minimum fines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Section 16 is introduced to clarify situations in which a film will be refused classification, after being reviewed by IMDA or FAC.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It entails no change in content standards for films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Sections 22 and 22A empower IMDA to approve or refuse approval of advertisements for films and set out the offences involving such advertisements.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Section 27 is amended to confine the Minister's powers to order FAC to only review films that IMDA has classified.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This clarifies the FAC's role as an appellate body for classification decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Section 38 introduces standard provisions so that corporations and unincorporated associations or partnerships are also liable for offences under the FA and not just individuals.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: MCI and IMDA's content regulatory approach reflects the community standards while providing more choices for consumers and protecting the young.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I will touch upon four main areas of the Bill, Mr Deputy Speaker: (a) formalisation of the Co-Classification Scheme; (b) appeals against IMDA’s decisions; (c) clarification on films classification; and (d) enhancements to IMDA’s investigation and enforcement powers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I applaud this move, as it is pro-business and in the interests of the consumer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, this move also helps strengthen capabilities within the media industry to better understand classification guidelines and processes, while consumers can get access to films more quickly.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I wanted to ask, since this scheme is optional, as films can still be sent to IMDA for classification, how has the response been from the industry in adopting this?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, from the IMDA point of view, I would like to understand why it is, in a way, "outsourcing" its classification responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The intent of the Films Bill is to safeguard content standards.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the safeguards in place to prevent the newly-formalised co-classification scheme from being abused?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Have there been examples of such cases since it was piloted?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Further, there is already an existing appeals process for film classification.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are there safeguards in place to prevent the abuse of these powers by IMDA?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For instance, could IMDA be lobbied by interest groups or could be put under pressure, to reclassify controversial films to give them either higher or lower ratings?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How do we ensure that this does not happen?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On FAC, currently, the FAC comprises a mix of individuals representing the community, creative, legal and education sectors, as well as academia.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can we make the composition more representative of the community?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will MCI or IMDA take suggestions from the industry for suitable nominations to FAC?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I spoke to members of the film community, and they would like to suggest increasing the transparency and accountability of the FAC's decisions and not just receive an opaque reply.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would MCI or IMDA be open to being more engaging with the industry on the FAC's decisions?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On appeals involving films with national security concerns, I am satisfied that the amendments in the Bill took into consideration that national security is one of the Government's core responsibilities, as the FAC may not be privy to the full extent of concerns from security agencies due to the sensitivity of information.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some of the community had asked whether FAC should be maintained as the appeal authority for films with national security concerns.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are concerns that if the Minister is to decide on such appeals, they may not be able to represent themselves and explain the context of their work.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, is it possible that the appellants be allowed to make in-person representations to the Minister, or the FAC is part of the Minister's consultation process?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will FAC be consulted before the Minister decides on the appeals involving national security and whether their inputs will be given weightage in this process?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Replacement of Not Allowed for all Ratings (NAR) with "Refused classification": a very small number of films that exceed acceptable community norms or are against public interest are not allowed for distribution or public exhibition.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Such films are currently determined to be NAR.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Under the new FA, such films would be refused classification by IMDA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Why is there such a change in terminology?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Is this change really necessary under the legal construct of the amended Act?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As I understand it, the NAR is just a simple change in terminology.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry confirm that there is no change to its meaning or application with the new "Refused Classification" terminology?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that there have only been two such films that have been classified as NAR or prohibited in the past.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the thresholds and how are the norms and boundaries of public interests defined?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Through my interactions with the local film industry, they are concerned that the new term "Refused Classification" could also be misunderstood by the wider international film community and affect the reputation of our filmmakers and films.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are also concerned that the term implies that the film is not viewed by IMDA prior to classification.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister probably has to watch many of these films to decide.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the industry be assured that all films will be viewed prior to being branded “Refused Classification”?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If the Minister decides on appeals of films that are “Refused Classification” for undermining national security, how will the appeals process for such films change from current procedures, where appeals are submitted to FAC under the existing FA?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These include powers to request information, such as documents, as well as interview persons and take statements for a suspected breach of FA or licence conditions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How has IMDA been enforcing against FA offences thus far, given the gaps in enforcement and investigation powers?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Have MCI or IMDA considered the merit of continuing with the existing enforcement framework where IMDA relies on the Police where it does not possess the requisite enforcement and investigation powers and what were the compelling reasons to make this change?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Has IMDA or the Police had to use without-warrant powers in the past?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If not, why are these powers, including the use of reasonable force in obtaining entry, necessary?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry clarify under what types of offences does the power of searching without warrant and to enter, search and seize evidence come into force?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the case where the offence is the illegal distribution of film, will items, such as film-making equipment – because by nature, filming is not an offence under the FA, only distribution is – or non-relevant items like handphones, computers, which are not related to the distribution and storage of evidence, be seized, too?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is the recourse for those affected in view of privacy concerns that personal and private content may be searched through by the authorities?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What kind of processes does IMDA put in place to ensure proper checks and balances when enforcement officers carry out enforcement activities, especially for entry and seizure without warrant?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the training and internal processes in place to ensure that the IMDA enforcement officers exercise the without-warrant powers and forced entry appropriately?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: IMDA sought consultation last year with the film community.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, in my speech, I would address some of these concerns that were put up by the filmmakers which were also addressed by my colleague, Mr Zaqy Mohamad, just now.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Some will seem repetitive, so do bear with me.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I will highlight three main areas of concerns.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The first area of concern pertains to whether several amendments may restrict the creativity boundaries and artistic space for the filmmakers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The second area is about the sweeping powers given to IMDA enforcement officers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The third area would pertain to the need to ensure due process and fairness in relation to the appeals process under FA.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Let us look at the first area of concern.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: There are several amendments to this Bill that I feel might potentially stifle the space for creativity and the artistic work by filmmakers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I note that there is no specification of what is the definition of "material prescribed" nor is there a definition of what is "against national security".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In turn, this may cause the film industry to self-censor on the kind of films that they may produce.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I, therefore, hope the Minister can provide some clarification or guidelines as to what constitutes a film that contains "material prescribed", or one that is "against national security".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: On the definition of "national security", I note that it is not impossible to provide some clarity on its contours.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Take, for example, the Public Order and Special Powers Bill that we debated just now.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill has specifically set out several situations that constitute "serious incident" that may affect public order and security.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Further, under the proposed section 15(5), the provision sets out several guidelines as to what will be taken into consideration in classifying a film.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Although section 15(5) does not strictly relate to issues of "national security" or "prescribed materials", it does show that it is possible, at the very least, to provide examples of what would be taken into account in reaching a particular classification decision.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Even if it is not possible to give a clear definition of what constitutes "prescribed materials" or what is “against national security”, at the very least, the Minister can set out what it will take into consideration in determining whether a film is against national security or contains those prescribed materials.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Such clarity is important to ensure a creative environment in which the film industry will not be inhibited by unknown legal perimeters and to cultivate an environment that encourages diverse narratives and perspectives to be explored through the films.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I agree with the Minister that, actually, films talk about what we are and who we are and are important cultural tenets of this society.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: On a related note, as regards the proposed section 16 which permits the Minister to refuse classification, I would like to clarify whether this means that the Minister would refuse classification of a film that falls under the proposed section 16, or does it mean that such a film will be given a "Refused Classification" rating?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Again, I think the way we put the terminology becomes very important so that it would not cause confusion.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This convenience has been welcomed by the businesses, mostly by the distributors, as it shortens the processing time when they can classify their own Parental Guidance Suggested (PG) or PG13 films, instead of waiting on the IMDA classification division.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, the film community is not just made up of these distributors.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, the scheme may not benefit filmmakers or consumers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As it is now in Singapore, some production companies are also distributors.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: One of them has just bought over even a cinema chain.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, a three-in-one production company, distributor and exhibitor.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Creators should be allowed to make works that can best express their stories and engage consumers and leave the regulatory and censorship monitoring to the authorities and be allowed to appeal if they think an age-restriction rating is too strict.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But, as we can see in several cases, the consumers are not well-served by this amendment, and can, in fact, be shortchanged by this.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This is because distributors are incentivised to cut out shots to achieve a lower age-restriction rating and, hence, reach possibly larger audiences.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But consumers may not be fully informed on what they are missing, even when they are still paying for full-price admission.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The fact that the film has been censored is usually not advertised on the promotional collaterals put out by the distributors and cinema operators.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, a rating that is displayed at the box office where consumers buy their tickets would usually be stated simply just as PG13 but, in fact, certain scenes may have been taken away.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, maybe it should be accurately reflected as "PG13  ".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, external CAs will be penalised if they classify it wrongly, hence, it will inadvertently lead to them being more conservative in the way they classify.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I want to now turn to the proposed sections 34 and 34A of the Bill which confers IMDA enforcement officers with intrusive and excessive powers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Fundamentally, I believe that such sweeping and intrusive powers should only be granted to the Police who are the custodians of law and order.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Moreover, I am concerned whether we are giving too much power to enforcement officers who, as compared to our Police, might not have the operational experience and expertise to effectively discharge such powers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I further note that under the proposed section 34(11), an enforcement officer may be assisted by other individuals in exercising enforcement powers under this Act.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is not clear from this section who such "other individuals" refer to, nor are such "other individuals" defined under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister clarify who these "other individuals" refer to?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Do such "other individuals" refer to IMDA licensing officers and/or classification officers or are they non-IMDA officers?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: What are the situations which the Minister would envisage the assistance of such other individuals, and can the Minister clarify what are the powers which such individuals can exercise while assisting enforcement officers in discharging their duties under the Act?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Apart from the fact that the enforcement and Police Officers are exercising sweeping powers, I am concerned that such powers may be exercised without a warrant under section 34A(2) if such officers suspect that certain offences under the Act are committed.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I note that under the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC), the Police may exercise its powers of search and seizure only when an arrestable offence is committed.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Some examples of an arrestable offence under our Penal Code include rioting and voluntarily causing grievous hurt.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I note that the offences under the FA are nowhere as severe or violent as the examples of arrestable offences which I have just cited.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Moreover, there is nothing in the FA nor in the amendments to this Bill which provides that the offences under the Act are arrestable.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I would like, therefore, to understand why, despite the fact that the offences under the Act are non-arrestable, and, despite the fact that these offences are not as severe as arrestable offences, then why enforcement officers and the Police are permitted to search and seize without warrant.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Moreover, what I feel is particularly egregious is the fact that an enforcement officer may exercise such intrusive powers without warrant, powers that are traditionally within the purview of the Police.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, I would like to understand what prompted the Government to provide for such a devolution of powers from the Police to enforcement officers and to potentially other undefined individuals?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: How do we ensure that the enforcement officers will not be over-zealous in their search for evidence such that the privacy of individuals is not infringed?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I turn now to the next area of concern, which is to ensure due process and fairness in the appeals process.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I am rather concerned that neither the FA nor the amendment provides that the appellant appealing a decision is guaranteed the right to be heard by either the Committee of Appeal or the Minister.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: With regard to appealing a decision which is to be heard by a Minister, the proposed 24A(3)(b) merely states that the Minister may consult any person before making his decision regarding the appeal.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: With regard to the appeal to be heard by the Committee of Appeal under the proposed section 24, the said section did not provide that the applicant has the right to be heard by the Committee.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Another concern that I have with the appeals process is with the composition of FAC.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Clause 12 of the Bill, which provides for the constitution of the Committee of Appeal, only provides that the number of members is of, at least 15, but not more than 21 members.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: To quote from one of the filmmakers in one of the discussions I had with her: "We, in the film community, do have valuable professional perspectives to contribute, as well as feedback rooted in civic and consumer rights".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that the appointment of the present Committee will end by June 2019.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I hope to understand from the Minister whether he would take into consideration to have a more diverse selection of members of the committee, including those from the film industry, when appointing the next Committee.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As a matter of ensuring due process and in fairness to the applicant, he or she should be aware of the basis on which his or her appeal is either upheld or dismissed.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Further, providing the grounds of decision also ensures that the decision-maker is held accountable.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I know that this has not been put up for amendment in this particular Bill.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, it is stated clearly in the Explanatory Statement that one of the purposes of this present amendment to the FA is for "excluding private exhibition, and the making and the reproduction of films".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In paragraph 2.15 of the IMDA's public consultation paper, it is stated that, I quote, "MCI/IMDA would like to clarify that the primary regulatory focus of the Films Act remains on the distribution and public exhibition of the films, as these activities have wider and more direct impact on consumers" – which was reiterated by the Minister earlier.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Moreover, under the proposed section 2(6), it is expressly stated that the private viewing alone of a film by an individual does not constitute exhibiting the film by the individual.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: To put it in context, take, for example, an individual who video-records a political rally.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The person then edits the video with a video-editing app by adding in some music and politically motivated slogans for his own personal viewing, or just to share this edited video privately with some of his friends.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If I am not mistaken, such a video may fall under the definition of a film provided under the proposed section 3 of the Bill and may constitute a party political film under the present section 2 of the FA.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: That said, I again would like to thank the Ministry for being very responsive throughout the public consultation period, and for taking seriously consideration of the feedback it received and also have to reconsider and amend certain parts of the amendment Bill in light of the feedback it received.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Now, with regard to my own fundamental position on one of the important amendments to this Bill – which is about co-classification – in 2014, IMDA actually wanted to propose a similar scheme for the arts sector.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The Term Licensing Scheme was proposed for arts groups to be able to have their own CAs to help co-classify productions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This was rejected by the Arts community, myself being one of them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: One of the fundamental issues I have with this co-classification scheme is this: that the censorship and regulation guidelines are set up by the authority.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, it should be the job of the authority to man the gates but for artists to submit it so that the authority can decide whether they want it, and whether they will classify it or not classify it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Market, societal and technological developments have changed videography and the consumption of films since the FA was last amended in 2009.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Several of the moves contained in these amendments should be welcomed for liberalising the media field and, in effect, encouraging the development of a vibrant media industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Dissolving the BFC and formalising the Co-Classification Scheme would help further shift the paradigm from knee-jerk censorship to age-appropriate classification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Amending the licensing framework to exclude private exhibition and the making and reproduction of films recognises the maturity of our society and the media industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It recognises that our citizens are more than able to make value judgements on what they watch and are not simpletons prone to being brainwashed and losing their moral compass.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are: (a) keeping up to date with technology and social norms; (b) the question of public interest; and (c) the regulatory risk of raids and seizures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The amendments contained in this Bill seek to update definitions and regulations so that they match the current common uses of media technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even the word, "film", has a new definition to keep up with the watching of films on mobile devices and through online streaming.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The problem is that the Bill is still very focused on the term "exhibit" as the main activity that it seeks to heavily regulate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The definition of "film" is very broad, referring not just to a cinematograph film, but any video recording or any form of recording with a moving visual image, including computer-generated image.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This covers a whole range of activities that do not fit the common sense of the word, "exhibit".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the Explanatory Statement of the Bill, "exhibit" is said to include "showing to any other individual content comprising, wholly or in part, moving images received on a computer monitor, television screen, mobile device or similar medium equipment appropriate for receiving that content, and where the delivery of the content is by a broadcasting service, telecommunications or other electronic transmission".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also said, "But an individual will not be regarded as exhibiting a film if the individual is watching a film alone and in private".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Given that a lot of people consume and share video recordings of one kind or another on their mobile devices on a daily basis, it would be good for the Minister to clarify the limits of "exhibit".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is important because such a wide definition can have a chilling effect on public discourse.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the Closing Note to the public consultation on the Bill, MCI/IMDA said that three things are sensitive subject matters: race, religion or politics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I strongly believe it is important to safeguard our racial and religious harmony and national security.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, to mark race, religion and politics as sensitive subject matters in themselves is to send mixed signals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Social norms have been evolving and Singaporeans seem prepared to discuss race, religion and politics more openly now in a civil manner.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For many decades, Singaporeans have been told that we should avoid discussions of issues related to race and religion because these are sensitive and explosive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Representations of race and religion in Singapore films tend to fall back on safe caricatures and common stereotypes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This does not help in encouraging mutual understanding and respect and may even reinforce racial and religious prejudices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In fact, it is for this very reason that the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) supported BRIDGE, partnering community groups in providing safe spaces to frankly discuss topics related to race and religion to strengthen our social fabric.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the launch in March 2017 of BRIDGE, a documentary film titled "Jihad Selfie" was shown to over 120 religious and community leaders, who then discussed the complexities of extremist self-radicalisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This demonstrates that films and the exhibition of films have an important role to play in building and shoring up our multiracialism and multiculturalism.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Difficult topics on race and religion should not be avoided by content producers, filmmakers and civil society and community groups.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It would be to our benefit that safe spaces, such as those supported by BRIDGE, could multiply through our society and without having to always depend on the Government’s oversight.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is important that the Government continue to safeguard racial and religious harmony, so there must be a balance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In MCI’s Closing Note, it is stated that the Ministry seeks "to encourage the development of a vibrant media industry, while ensuring that the content does not undermine Singapore's racial and religious harmony, national security or the public interest".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is clear that it is crucial for racial and religious harmony and national security to be safeguarded by the Government.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But "public interest" is a vague term, much like "exhibit", which, when unlimited in meaning, would give IMDA draconian powers to ban any film or video recording it deems as against "public interest".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the term refers to social norms concerning sexuality and sexual identities, then it should be clearly stated as such.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Minister clarify what does "public interest" mainly refer to?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am asking this because MCI/IMDA said in the Closing Note that politics is a sensitive subject matter on par with race and religion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think this is a terribly outdated view, especially when the Government has been trying to encourage a more engaged citizenry and greater public understanding of our political system and sense of history.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The SG50 commemorations and the passing of Mr Lee Kuan Yew appear to be watershed events in this regard, with a more politically conscious public interested in how the country could and should be run in the context of global trends and world events.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: MCI/IMDA also said in the Closing Note that "social norms could evolve such that lower ratings become more appropriate".

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think our social norms regarding political discussion and expression have evolved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Almost 10 years now, from 2009, the absence of an update is conspicuous.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because if they had, then the amendments in this Bill should reflect it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Other than politics, there have been a greater interest in different interpretations of Singapore's history in recent years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It would be good for the country if we could depoliticise history and open the history to multiple but fair interpretations of it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is no doubt that the events in the 1950s and 1960s are very important for understanding how we have become who we are.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is because they are very important that they should be divorced from the politics of today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The politics in the past should not be conflated with the politics of today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It was a different context with different actors then.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For our sense of history to be credible and our national identity to be deep and authentic, there is a need for society to discuss, debate and understand the different aspects and perspectives of this history.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Only then can we truly appreciate why different actors did the things they did without excusing or glorifying them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A balanced view of history results not from monotonous stories reflecting some kind of officially sanctioned history, but from many fair and honest stories told from multiple perspectives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I come now to the third and last issue of IMDA having powers to do raids and seizures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When the amendment Bill was first put out for public consultation last December, it raised concerns from the public that IMDA officers would have too much power and that the exercise of these powers would erode public confidence in the regulation regime for films.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is good that MCI/IMDA responded to the public uproar by extending the public consultation period and refining the amendments to clarify the powers of entry and search without warrant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Though now circumscribed, these powers are still very expansive and, if used in a heavy-handed manner and liberally, would erode public confidence in the regulation regime for films and thus negatively affect the development of the media industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, would the Minister clarify that these powers would, indeed, be used in the spirit of exception, as a "nuclear option" of last resort when speed is of the essence in securing evidence of the offence committed?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Third, would the Minister clarify that all care would be taken to ensure that private data in the seized equipment and devices would be protected, secured and returned to the affected persons?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government must, however, ensure that the enhanced regulation regime does not cause a chilling effect on the media field or erode public confidence in the regulation process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clarifications are needed in this respect with regard to the definition of "exhibit" and the approach to regulating films containing the subject matters of race, religion and politics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is also a need to exercise the powers to search and seize without warrant with extreme care, as these pose a major regulatory risk – one wrong move could backfire on the development of a vibrant media industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In closing, I would like to leave behind one word.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The word is "gingerly", as I hope the Government would regulate films "gingerly".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And it was my late Daddy who always taught me to speak up, to question, to always focus on solutions and to try my best, no matter what.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But films probably played the second most important role in shaping my life, shaping the person I am today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At 14, I watched a documentary, or film called "Gorillas in the Mist" that told the true life story of Dian Fossey, an American lady who gave up her good life in America to go to Africa to study and save gorillas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That movie singlehandedly changed my life and probably my Mommy's, too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I watched that movie with her and, halfway through, I turned to her and said, "Mommy, I want to be just like Dian once I grow up".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mommy freaked out at the end of the movie because Dian was murdered by the poachers, and she thought this was probably what her son wanted to do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I spent the last 17 years of my life protecting animals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Like Dian, I, too, studied primates, but gibbons and not gorillas, and, thankfully, unlike Dian, I have not been killed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Films, continue to shape my life – from the food I eat, to the places I visit and to the father I am today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And so, the amendments we are proposing today will not only have an impact on just the films industry, but on all of us, on our society because, ultimately, we are not just what we eat but what we watch.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do believe I met up the same filmmakers that Member Kok Heng Leun met as well because some of the clarifications that I will say will be similar to his.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They have emphasised to me the need to have checks and balances in the regulatory and enforcement framework.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Films, with their transformative powers, are a crucial part of our nation's arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is important to protect the ability of filmmakers to tell their stories openly, honestly and with integrity, and to preserve the right of audiences to enjoy those stories.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But at the same time, there is also a need to have regulations in place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Before raising my questions for clarifications, I would, first, like to commend IMDA for engaging with the filmmakers and the public in their review of the FA, which started in May last year and involved several meetings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The filmmakers that I met highlighted to me several changes in the final Bill that resulted from IMDA's consultation process on the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a good example of how the public can be constructively engaged in the law-making process.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that, presently, filmmakers are given the opportunity to present their case before the FAC.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Filmmakers I have spoken with have indicated that this current practice satisfies them that the decision was made in accordance with due process even if the appeal does not succeed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will this positive practice be maintained, and will filmmakers continue to have the opportunity to present their case before the Committee of Appeal and/or the Minister in an appeal against a classification decision?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While there is no guarantee of such a right to audience even under the current FA, the opportunity to be heard is an important procedural safeguard.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, would the minutes of the Committee of Appeal's deliberations on a classification and grounds for decision on the appeal be published?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Similarly, while a decision of a Minister on a matter of national security is deemed to be final, will the Minister be providing reasons for his decision?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I check with the Minister if we will be including more members of the film community and civil society who can provide professional perspectives and feedback reflecting civic and consumer concerns?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify how the proposed category of "Refused Classification" differs from the current rating of "Not Allowed for All Ratings" (NAR)?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Filmmakers also wanted clarifications that the BFC will watch and assess the films that are subsequently deemed to be "Refused Classification" notwithstanding the language, which may be understood as suggesting that the film will not be reviewed at all?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I would also like to seek further clarification on the scope of those categories.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify what would constitute a "prohibited film" and "a film against national security" respectively?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister also shed some light on the type of films that might be refused classification under the catch-all provision "contains any material prescribed" that is not currently already covered by the first four categories?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, what is the rationale behind providing for such powers to deal with matters of national security under the FA when there are other pieces of legislation, such as the Penal Code, the Internal Security Act (ISA) and the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act that deal with matters that might threaten national security?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I also find out if we will be publishing the reasons and bases for the classification decisions by IMDA and registered film CAs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Clearly communicating the grounds for decisions ensures accountability and transparency.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, one concern raised by filmmakers is that an external film CA hired by the distributors may be incentivised to cut out shots to achieve lower age-restriction ratings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Film reviewers would have reviewed and recommended the uncut version, while audiences only see the cut version and may not be aware of what they have missed out, since the full advisory is only available on the IMDA online classification database.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This could be done, as suggested earlier, on the classification label that IMDA must issue under section 18(1)(b).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, a PG13 film could be advertised as PG13 (Edited).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, sections 34 and 34A extend certain enforcement powers of an enforcement officer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are granted special enforcement powers that may be exercised without warrant.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that these officers will have powers to conduct search and seizure, what kind of training will the officer be required to undergo to ensure that they are able to exercise these extensive powers responsibly?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note the Minister has said they will be trained by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under sections 34 and 34A, enforcement officers will have the power to seize anything which the officer reasonably suspects is evidential material.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister provide examples of what can and cannot be seized under this provision, given that films do not clearly take the form of just film reels or DVDs as they did in the past, and can now be stored on all kinds of storage devices?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This would seem to cover mobile phones, personal tablets, laptops, computers and thumbdrives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amendments would implicate everyone who owns a camera and storage devices, not just filmmakers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that the special enforcement powers of enforcement officers allow them to enter a place "using such force as is reasonably necessary to obtain entry".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand from speaking with individuals within the film industry that this provision is intended for use against errant distributors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister confirm that this is the intention behind this provision?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Have there been instances where forced entries have been required in dealing with distributors?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the amendments bring the streaming of films under the ambit of the FA?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I can see how much they have impacted my daughter Ella as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While she has only watched four films so far, Paddington, Madagascar, The Lion King and Ant Bully, but I am pretty sure that, one day, Ella, too, will freak me out while we are watching a film, like how my Mommy was freaked out by me.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I run the Asian business of a multinational media company, Fremantlemedia International.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The first is the class licensing requirement for video games retailers to enhance the protection of minors.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: However, Mr Deputy Speaker, this amendment only applies to physical copies of video games.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Increasingly, I have discovered as a parent of a teenager, children buy their games online.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: What this means is that platforms like gaming consoles and apps are the most common transaction platforms for upgrades and purchases of new games.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Parents' Paypal or credit card accounts are required for such purchases.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These payment details are usually stored after the initial purchase, with authorisation necessary for subsequent purchases.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The onus, therefore, must be on parents to scrutinise the games that their children purchase online and to make sure that the games are suitable for their kids.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I know of many parents who, because of their hectic schedules, are happy to approve these purchases without due assessment.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I urge parents to monitor their children’s online purchases until such time when laws governing such online purchases are amended to adequately protect minors.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Co-classification of content is not a new phenomenon and has been tested in several countries and adopted successfully.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The scheme, Sir, is a pro-business and consumer move.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It is pro-business and driven by the commercial market.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Some quarters have commented that co-classification could lead to self-censorship, so that distributors and exhibitors could show the films to a bigger audience.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is not necessarily true as I think we need to give our audiences a little bit more credit.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These are commercial decisions, and the market tends to regulate itself.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: One example is the 2007 film, "Lust, Caution".

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The distributor originally wanted to release the film as an edited No Children below 16 (NC16) version but, after public feedback, released the original film under the Restricted to Those over 21 (R21) rating.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The distributor decided to show several versions of the film to attract a bigger audience.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: And in other cases, distributors will tend to have just the one edited version because of cost considerations.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The co-classification scheme also allows for PG13 and below titles to hit the market more quickly.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is pro-consumer, as Singaporean audiences can be the first to watch these films.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It has also the desired effect of shortening the window for piracy.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This move allows for producers of films and exhibitors to engage in more robust debate about classifications, and this inevitably will build stronger industry capability and better understanding of classification guidelines and processes.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Most importantly, Mr Deputy Speaker, this scheme is optional as films can still be sent to IMDA for classification if the distributors want to.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Another important amendment to the Act is the granting of relevant enforcement and investigation powers to IMDA.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There has been understandably a bit of a furore over this proposed amendment.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: However, Mr Deputy Speaker, I think that when it comes to films that could undermine our social fabric, disrupt our racial and religious harmony as well as national security, these investigative and enforcement powers, carried out with discretion and attention to detail, will be a very small price to pay.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: What is of most concern for some quarters is the granting of powers to IMDA officers to enter and search premises without warrant and seize equipment, in particular equipment used to procure a livelihood, such as professional cameras used for filmmaking and also personal equipment, such as laptops and phones.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The issue here is the possible abuse of power and the privacy of the individuals being searched.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There is much concern that the proposed powers of search and entry without warrant could be open to abuse.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: However, I would like to ask the Minister for more clarity on the following as many of my Parliamentary colleagues have done just now.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: While I understand that these officers will undergo training with the Home Team, what is the nature and duration of this training?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a process for a senior authority in the Ministry to assess the facts of the case and to authorise the raid?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, what is the recourse for people who have been the victim of these raids who may have been wrongly implicated?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that the Minister can share these details as they will allay some public fears.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: One suggestion from interest groups is that the FAC be made up of nominees from all its stakeholder groups.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This, in my view, could make the regulatory process an arduous one with different interest groups lobbying their representatives to influence the Committee’s decisions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I am in complete support of this amendment.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Given the uniqueness of our social fabric, which is dependent on racial harmony, national security could be undermined by films that promote or reflect values and tenets contrary to this.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that the Minister will also consult FAC before making his decision, and this should allay the concerns of the filmmaking community.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Take, for example, Netflix, which was once regarded primarily as an online-streaming platform that provided traditional film production companies another alternative channel for exhibition.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
