text: With funding and rapid development and growth, Netflix now produces its own films and dramas, which it shows on its own platform, thus completely circumventing traditional distribution and exhibition channels.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In light of such disruptive evolution to the film and media industry, in light of changing social norms, it is timely that the Government review the FA to ensure that it remains relevant in the age of digital media.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first area is the co-classification of films.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This provision is, in principle, a positive one, as it signifies a more collaborative and consultative approach towards film classification.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This should benefit distributors and audiences in the long run because of the wider range of views incorporated as part of the classification process and the increased number of film industry professionals who now have been trained to classify films.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I do have some clarifications that I hope that the Minister can help me with.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, while the Bill describes the procedures to apply to be a CA, it does not specify the type of qualifications one needs to have before application and who will approve these applications.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that any required qualifications will not be too narrowly defined and the approval process not too tightly regulated.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, I understand that the CA scheme might not be applied to all categories of films.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Minister please explain why that would be so, and if we could work towards eventually allowing CAs to classify films up to a higher classification level, similar to those currently classified by the authorities?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to ask under what circumstances the authorities would override or reclassify a film already classified by a CA.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This topic of reclassification was raised by my colleague, the hon Member Mr Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My concern is that if the authorities were to do this too often, this could result in the public perception that the authorities only prefer CAs to “rubber-stamp” ratings in accordance with the authorities' pre-approved guidelines and standards.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second area, Sir, is the appeals process.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Any appeals for reclassification are currently being decided by FAC.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am supportive of this change as it ensures that FAC can incorporate more diversity and FAC gets refreshed on a regular basis.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While such structured refreshment of the FAC ensures that new perspectives are being constantly brought in, I feel that the authorities can consider emulating the practices on corporate boards by renewing the tenure of some members beyond three years, provided that it can justify why the tenure of these members should be extended.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This ensures that there is a good mix and overlap of new members and experienced ones, which will be useful should there be a need to rely on experience and historical knowledge when deciding on appeals.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On this note, could the Minister also shed more light on the composition of the FAC and the process as to how members are selected, and does the Government plan to engage the industry and films community to solicit nominees for the committee?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that in drawing some of the FAC members from the industry, this will be critical in ensuring that the committee has the endorsement and support from the community and also helps strengthen the buy-in for decisions that the FAC would ultimately have to make.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The third area, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, is that of films and national security.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We heard this debated in quite a few speeches before mine.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, I think it is fair to say that I understand the concept of creative freedom in the media and why it is important for us to get the balance right, between allowing space and licence for artistic creativity to grow and blossom but not allowing carte blanche such that anyone can come up with a media product in the name of art or creative freedom that could have a damaging effect on society or on the community.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my opinion, the Government has been progressive in its attitude and policies towards media over time since I began my career as a media professional in the early 1990s.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that things will continue to change both for those who produce media and those who consume it to reflect changing societal norms, consumer tastes and preferences and technological advancements and developments.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But these changes need to be calibrated and measured and there are boundaries that should never be crossed.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While most films do not openly preach violence against the community, we cannot ignore that certain plotlines could contain innuendos that may injure the feelings of some communities, or some films could have thinly veiled messages that are disparaging to a particular religion or could be viewed as legitimising certain extremist views.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I was also heartened to hear the Minister say earlier that he will seek the views and consult the FAC before arriving at a decision.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I hope that the Minister will be willing to go even one step further and share with the FAC or even the public, the reasons as to why he would have made a particular decision regarding a film that might be deemed as a threat to national security.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such transparency would not only be illuminating; it would also be educational.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nevertheless, I am aware of the sentiments held by certain members of the film and media industry that the amendments to the FA may stifle artistic freedom and creative expression and lead to self-censorship.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe this was also raised by the hon Member Kok Heng Leun in his speech earlier.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, one could make the point that having those boundaries might present certain challenges that would inspire and motivate the artist to achievements that might not have been possible had those boundaries not been there in the first place.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, legendary award-winning producer and writer Lorne Michaels was quoted as saying: "To me there's no creativity without boundaries.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If you're gonna write a sonnet, it's 14 lines, so it's solving the problem within the container".

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, in the spirit of creativity within the container, I end my speech in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat, you wanted to make a clarification?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: He cited a closing note to our public consultation where race, religion, politics were mentioned as sensitive subject matters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, I want to confirm with Assoc Prof Daniel Goh if my understanding is correct, that the section that he was referring to refers to co-classification?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, for that section, Sir, we laid out what we want to do to work in partnership with industry and with film CAs to co-classify films.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Such content could be sensitive, depending on how they are presented.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are, hence, starting the scheme with other categories of films.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think it is important, and I would like to clarify, we should not quote that specific line out of context.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: IMDA has and will continue to classify films and provide age-appropriate ratings and consumer advisories so that Singaporeans, both young and old, can make informed viewing choices.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There is no lack of avenues to raise issues and to debate in real life or online in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This includes the films industry making, viewing and disseminating films with political content under IMDA's classification system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our safeguards are intended to protect public interest against egregious content.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is how we have found a balance between freedom of speech, creative expression and safeguarding our collective greater good.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is not one or the other, neither "free for all" nor "nothing at all".

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They thereby have the risk of harming our political discourse.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But not all films with political content are PPFs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There are, in fact, many films that deal with political content and serious issues in ways that inform Singaporeans, that both enrich our media space and our political space.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We should not compare PPFs to other films.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They are a different category of films, given the impact that they could have on the integrity of our elections as well as the broader political discourse in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The issue of PPFs is a basic judgement, whether it is better to debate political issues with words and logic, or with images and emotions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Given the harm that PPFs can cause to rational political discourse, we believe there is strong reason, and it is prudent, to maintain the current provisions against the making of PPFs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And let me assure the House that IMDA will continue to be judicious in administering the provisions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I agree with him that is important to know our history.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we also need safeguards to prevent distortion and misrepresentation of facts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There will be different accounts of the formative events of our nationhood, but there are also basic facts which are not matters of opinion, and which successors and sympathisers of the protagonists at the time are still trying to deny.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Not all narratives are equally truthful and valid.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I believe Assoc Prof Daniel Goh may be referring to the two prohibited films under section 35: Zahari's 17 Years and Dr Lim Hock Siew.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The two men were involved in communist activities and had posed a threat to the interests and security of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The films made baseless accusations against the authorities and undermine public confidence in the Government.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This has nothing to do with the politics today.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But the stance we take with regard to these actions by certain individuals in the past, to distort the facts and to use false portrayals to exculpate their guilt, can have an impact on what others may do in the future which could then affect our national security and public safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I will try and respond with creativity within the container.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The majority of them, Sir, have expressed support for the amendments, and raised interesting views and questions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I will address their views in five broad areas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is because the classification process is faster and cheaper for participating companies which will only pay a flat fee per film or video title rather than a fee based on the title's duration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad also asked why IMDA was outsourcing its classification duties.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Instead, as I have just explained, the co-classification scheme aims to help our films industry to distribute film and video titles more quickly and to save costs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is one of the ways in which we will develop and grow our films industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Darryl David also asked about the potential challenges in implementing the co-classification scheme, and the safeguards in place to address misclassification risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, the prospective film CAs will be required to attend formal training and pass mandatory tests before qualifying for registration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Film CAs must also fulfil an annual retraining requirement and, when in doubt, they can consult IMDA on a film's appropriate rating.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will continue to classify films that exceed the PG13 rating.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will also classify certain categories of films regardless of rating, such as films intended for film festivals and those that deal with matters of race or religion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Third, IMDA will conduct regular checks on co-classified film titles and reclassify those that are misclassified.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The relevant company will have to replace the classification labels with the right rating and bear the associated costs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will carefully consider the facts and circumstances of any case before determining the appropriate step, including whether there is intentional misclassification, the severity of the misclassification, and the film CA's track record.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Possible regulatory action includes warnings and financial penalties.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The companies involved will also be penalised if they are found to have had a role in the misclassification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, Sir, all regulatory steps will be administrative, rather than criminal in nature.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As Mr Darryl David said, co-classification is, indeed, a collaborative effort with the industry, to ensure that films and videos meant for distribution and public exhibition are rated in line with the film classification guidelines.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Film CAs have to classify the films with reference to the film classification guidelines, which is no different from what IMDA does today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The safeguards in place will help to minimise misclassification risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We do not believe it will stifle the creative space for the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Darryl David also asked why co-classification would only apply to films up to PG13.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will consider whether to allow co-classification beyond PG13 in time, as the industry grows more familiar with the classification guidelines.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Both Mr Louis Ng and Mr Kok Heng Leun spoke about the prospect of consumers missing the uncut film should film CAs edit films to qualify them for lower ratings and asked if we could require all edited films to be expressly listed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Decisions on whether to edit a film and what film versions to screen are purely commercial ones made by film distributors or exhibitors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Some do release different versions for different audiences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Another example is the film "Attack on Titan", where two versions were screened in 2015, one rated M18 and the other edited for NC16.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In these two cases, the distributor decided to screen different versions, so that the films were viewed more widely.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, Members also spoke about the changes in IMDA's regulatory scope.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While it is true that online video games purchases are rising, as Mr Ganesh Rajaram noted, these often require credit card or other online payment methods that might mitigate the risk of underage consumers buying games with mature content without their parents’ consent.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, in contrast with online games, anyone can walk into physical stores and buy age-restricted games today without proving their age.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Louis Ng asked what the intent was in regulating the public exhibition of films that are digitally transmitted, and if this amendment would bring the streaming of films under the FA's ambit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The amendments are to ensure that the public exhibition of films is regulated under the FA, whether they are screened from a recording or from a digital transmission.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked if several scenarios would be considered public exhibition or otherwise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, if you are watching a movie on a mobile device in a Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station and someone peers over your shoulder to watch the same movie, that, Sir, is not considered public exhibition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Louis Ng asked about the new terminology, "Refused Classification", and whether the film would be viewed by IMDA before making such a decision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The short answer is that this is simply a change in terminology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, a film is "Not Allowed for all Ratings" (NAR) when it exceeds the film classification guidelines and is not suitable for distribution and public exhibition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, it is often not clear to people if NAR is a rating or not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, Sir, there is no change to IMDA's classification process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will continue to review the film and provide reasons for its rating or its decision to refuse classification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This would be the same for film CAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, section 15 of the Bill requires IMDA to view a film before it decides to refuse classification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA must also give reasons for deciding as such.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Going forward, these elements would be prescribed in regulations, and the provision cited enables it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will be transparent, as they will need to be published in the Gazette.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Third, Members also commented on the amendments to strengthen the classification and appeals process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Darryl David asked why IMDA needed film reclassification powers, since there is already an existing appeals process for film classification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA may also reclassify older films when there are relevant changes to the film classification guidelines, so that their ratings are up to date.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad also asked if there are safeguards in place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will have to weigh such feedback against the film classification guidelines, which help to ensure consistency in standards applied to all film content.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For contentious films, IMDA will also seek the views of the Films Consultative Panel (FCP), which comprises a cross-section of Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Such decisions by IMDA are also appealable to the FAC.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Darryl David as well as Mr Louis Ng and Mr Kok Heng Leun also asked several questions, including what would constitute a film against national security and how the new appeals process for such films would be like.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As I have mentioned earlier, national security is one of the Government’s core responsibilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We cannot outsource or delegate our responsibility to safeguard the security of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Considerations of national security include what would be detrimental to the continued existence of the country, its ability to exercise its sovereign rights, and the safety and security of its citizens and their way of life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Minister will also consult the FAC for its views before making his decision on the appeal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We do not disagree with Mr Kok Heng Leun that it would be useful to set out some considerations broadly, which I have done here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But, Sir, given the complex nature of national security matters, the prudent approach would be to avoid binding this in legislation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In refusing classification, let me assure Members again that IMDA has been and will continue to provide grounds for its decisions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Should there be appeals for films with national security concerns, I envisage that we will adopt an appeals process similar to existing Ministerial appeals, where the appellant and IMDA would be given due opportunity to make their respective cases to the Minister via written submissions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Where possible, the Minister will also provide the appellant with the grounds of his decision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Darryl David further asked about the rationale for the provisions that deal with films that are against national security, given existing laws, such as the ISA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The FA governs the regulation of films, regardless of the content theme or concern.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It provides the films industry and the public with a single point of reference and clarity on the regulation of films in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is a practical approach, given that any one film can contain multiple content themes or concerns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The FA also allows for a calibrated approach, depending on the nature and gravity of any undesirable content.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, films that are refused classification for exceeding classification guidelines are not allowed for distribution and public exhibition, but private viewing is allowed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, it will also be an offence to possess films that are prohibited under section 35.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We agree with Mr Darryl David that experience is important, too.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There is thus also a mix of newer and more experienced members, so that the FAC brings in new perspectives while maintaining an understanding of past decisions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The appointment process also considers nominations from various community groups, such as the Council for the Development of the Singapore Malay/Muslim Community (MENDAKI) and the Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The FAC's role is to hear appeals involving film classification, which takes reference from our community norms and values.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The FAC, therefore, has to reflect the range of perspectives that make up our society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Kok Heng Leun asked several questions about the FAC.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I also understand that the FAC would consider allowing appellants to present in person, too, before forming its views when it is consulted by the Minister on appeals regarding films with national security concerns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Films are prohibited under section 35 of the FA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is intended for films with the most egregious content, where even possession of the films would be contrary to public interest.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Examples of such content include films that advocate violence or films that threaten racial or religious harmony, the broader fabric of our society or public confidence in our institutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This section ensures that we have some safeguards against the most egregious content, to protect larger societal interests, even as we have moved away from censorship towards classification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fourth, Sir, I thank all hon Members who spoke about the extension of IMDA's enforcement and investigation powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked how IMDA has been enforcing against FA offences, given the current gaps in enforcement and investigation powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Currently, Sir, IMDA seeks the assistance of the Police, for instance, to investigate offences involving unclassified films when they are discovered and seized.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Louis Ng asked if IMDA has used without-warrant powers in the past, including the use of reasonable force to obtain entry, and if extending these powers are really necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun also asked about the rationale for these powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, I would clarify that without-warrant powers are not new.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA already has these powers for some offences, such as those involving unclassified films.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA has also been circumspect in invoking these powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They are meant for serious offences and for situations where IMDA has to act quickly in order to secure evidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA enforcement officers have entered business premises to seize unclassified films intended for distribution or exhibition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, people have generally cooperated and allowed access, after IMDA enforcement officers identified themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, IMDA has not had to use forced entry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But these powers are still necessary, as we cannot expect compliance in every instance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA has to be able to respond to a broad range of enforcement scenarios to be able to protect the public interest, but it has been and will continue to be circumspect in invoking these powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Kok Heng Leun, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Ganesh Rajaram and Mr Darryl David – in fact, everyone who spoke – also asked about IMDA's enforcement officers – their training, the extent and limit of their powers, and how IMDA would ensure that they exercise their powers responsibly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Their feedback, in fact, has been very useful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On enforcement, it has helped us to gain better appreciation of the concerns about without-warrant powers for entry, search and seizure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I have explained the egregious nature of prohibited films earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, we have also limited the exercise of these powers to IMDA's enforcement officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These officers currently already have to and will continue to attend and pass the Home Team Investigation Courses where they receive both classroom and practical training alongside Home Team officers in areas, such as (a) powers of entry, search and seizure, (b) collation of evidence, (c) recording of statements, and (d) preparation of investigation reports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are three phases of training with the Home Team: three weeks of basic training, one week of intermediate training and one week of advanced training, with annual refresher courses for all officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The enforcement officers are also security-vetted and the majority have prior experience in law enforcement agencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To Mr Kok Heng Leun’s question of which "other individuals" may assist IMDA officers in exercising the enforcement powers under the Act, this refers to Auxiliary Police Officers and information technology (IT) forensic engineers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It does not refer to other IMDA officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I would like to reassure Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Kok Heng Leun and Assoc Prof.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Daniel Goh that only items used in the commission of the offences would be seized.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: What is seized, of course, will depend on the specific offence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, for unlicensed public exhibition, IMDA officers are likely to seize the storage medium where the film is kept but not the projector or the exhibitor’s mobile phone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For distribution of unclassified films, the officers will only seize the copies of films being displayed or intended for distribution, but not personal items, such as the distributor’s mobile phone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: During the investigation of seized items, only materials that are relevant to the offence will be flagged as evidence, while the rest will be protected and will not be disclosed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is similar to conducting a physical search where enforcement officers will have to go through the storage space before extracting what is relevant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA's interest would only be on materials that serve as evidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have also provided an avenue for owners to challenge seizures of their items in Court.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Generally, IMDA will return seized items after investigations conclude.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Kok Heng Leun also asked whether we could continue with this current arrangement of relying on the Police in areas where IMDA does not possess the necessary powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It has the necessary domain expertise, and its officers also understand and appreciate the work of the media and films industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Extending IMDA's powers to close the enforcement and investigative gaps will enable IMDA to administer the Act effectively.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It will also allow the Police to focus on the other threats to security and law and order.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I believe this approach is in the best interest of both the films industry and Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Ganesh Rajaram and Mr Louis Ng also asked how IMDA will ensure that these powers are exercised responsibly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Verification is done to assess and ascertain the veracity of information received on potential offences committed and/or the identity of the potential offender.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Enforcement action will only be authorised if a prima facie case is established.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The senior IMDA enforcement officer will also be apprised of the operational plan and the rules of engagement, before any action is taken.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would also like to reassure Mr Rajaram that any person who deliberately gives false information to mislead IMDA to initiate enforcement actions would be committing an offence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, enforcement actions are undertaken by a team of enforcement officers, led by an experienced team leader.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: New or less experienced officers do not carry out enforcement actions on their own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Third, to safeguard against abuse, each enforcement officer is issued with an authorisation card that is distinct from the general IMDA staff passes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is spelt out in the Bill that enforcement officers must identify themselves if asked, failing which, entry can be refused.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fourth, an established whistleblowing policy is also in place where members of the public can lodge complaints of abuse.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA takes the abuse of enforcement powers very seriously.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Depending on the severity of the accusation and the evidence given, IMDA may deploy the accused officer to an administrative post during the investigation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If the allegations are true, internal disciplinary procedures will apply, including the prospect of dismissal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun asked why the making and reproduction of Party Political Films (PPFs) would remain an offence under the FA or, more broadly, why there is no amendment to the PPF provisions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh also asked about norms regarding politics in films.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And, Sir, by a quirk of history, I was on the other side of the House debating the same Bill on 27 February 1998.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As Mr Louis Ng shared, films can be emotive and powerful and shape one's worldview for a long time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is one thing for "Gorillas in the Mist" to inspire someone to devote his life to animal welfare, but another thing for distorted or sensationalised films to undermine a democracy and alter the course of a country forever.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Film, Sir, is not an ideal medium for political debate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Serious political issues could be sensationalised or distorted to evoke emotional rather than rational reactions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Films do not allow for effective rebuttals and there is a risk that political debates on serious matters could be reduced to a contest where parties and candidates promote themselves, attack others, or mislead voters through slick commercials and slanted presentations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We should thus not compare PPFs to other films.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They are a different category of films, given the impact they could have on the integrity of our elections, as well as the broader political discourse.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is, therefore, prudent to retain the provisions, so that we can continue to ensure that political debates in Singapore remain grounded in fact, for the greater and longer-term good of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, Sir, I would like to reassure Mr Kok Heng Leun that IMDA will continue to be judicious in administering these provisions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I just want to clarify that most artists do not make work in order to express artistic freedom.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think artists make work because they pick up on things that they think are of great concern to them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: That is why when they bring up something of concern, sometimes it may not fall within the comfort of certain particular groups of the society.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: A lot of the artistic work, while it starts from within the container, the intention is then to redraw the container or even get out of the container.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Kuo Pao Kun would always say, and I paraphrase, "Know the frame where you are in, so that you can break away from the frame to create new possibilities".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The last thing that I would like to address to the Minister is that I really hope that the Minister, whenever there is an appeal, especially for those unclassifiable, that the Minister see the filmmaker face-to-face.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think that will make the appeal process much more genuine and the conversations and dialogues much more in-depth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is really to allow some distributors to co-classify.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But it means that you can also make a film for any of the classification ratings that are available out there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If anything, from the distributors' point of view, it is a lot more efficient for them to bring their films to the market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But I agree with the hon Member that creativity is important because we want to continue to build our films industry to be dynamic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Most of the processes, if not all, we will basically deal with the agencies and for the agencies who are involved to give us their submissions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I think we will retain that for the moment and we allow it to work out and see how it works and then we will evolve from there and learn from the experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Deputy Speaker, two clarifications for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: So, when the Senior Minister of State said the phrase about race, religion and politics being taken, you know, that they are not sensitive subject matters because you are taking it out of context from it being put in the closing note on co-classification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: So, would the Senior Minister of State, therefore, agree with me that these subject matters are therefore not sensitive in themselves and Singaporeans therefore should be more open to discussing them in a civil matter, of course, in safe spaces?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And a filmmaker should be encouraged actually to produce content so that they can spark off discussions amongst Singaporeans about these subject matters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I did not mention those two prohibited films because I have not watched them because they are prohibited.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And that is precisely the problem, I think, because I would have wanted to watch them to make the judgement myself that, you know, these films are not good because they promote violence and so on and so forth, to overthrow the Government, and so on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: But the problem is precisely that censorship has alerted me to these films.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: And that is how I knew about these two films.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The publicity that surrounds the prohibition, the censorship and the banning of these films actually attracted me to these films.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The first point, I do not think I said that race, religion and politics are not sensitive issues.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think what I clarified earlier was that I asked Assoc Prof Goh whether he was referring to the closing note in which he quoted the remarks from IMDA and MCI, and whether that remark that he was referring to actually came from the section in the closing note touching on co-classification.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That was my clarification to Assoc Prof Goh and he has confirmed that that was where he saw that phrase.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That was the basis of my clarification earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The point that Assoc Prof Goh made about then was should we have films that touch on race, religion and politics to raise awareness, to generate discussion?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that was the point that he asked.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Certainly, I think we do have many of such films.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In fact, not too long ago, our Parliamentary colleague, Dr Janil Puthucheary, was involved in two films with Channel NewsAsia touching on race and religion.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And there are many other films by filmmakers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Both the filmmakers who are working on films with political content, films touching on race, on religion, I think we can find plenty of examples.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: What I mentioned earlier was that these films are allowed but they will go through IMDA's classification system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Some may be given, depending on the content.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I want to assure Assoc Prof Goh and the House that these powers will be exercised in a careful and judicious manner.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Certain regulations have not been amended because the fundamental nature of our multiracial and multi-religious society has not changed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And, indeed, this is something that we want to preserve and protect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I thank all hon Members for their views and their support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As I have mentioned earlier, we will always evolve and we always look for future amendments if we have to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But this is always something which is a work-in-progress.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On that note, Sir, I beg to move, "That Parliament immediately resolve itself into a Committee on the Bill".
